title: Epsilon-Optimal Strategy
body_html:
Epsilon-Optimal Strategy

Given $\varepsilon>0$, a row strategy $x \in \Delta(I)$ is maxmin $\varepsilon$-optimal if its guarantee meets at least $\operatorname{val}(A) - \varepsilon$: $$ \min_{j \in J} E_A(x, j) \ge \operatorname{val}(A) - \varepsilon. $$ A $0$-optimal strategy is an optimal strategy. The dual definition (a column strategy $y$ is $\varepsilon$-optimal when $\max_{i \in I} E_A(i, y) \le \operatorname{val}(A) + \varepsilon$) applies to player 2.

References

  • [MFoGT, Def. 2.2.6] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. Epsilon-optimal and optimal strategies.
